transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE); Priya Sharma (Redwood SE); Jordan Lee (ZenithCorp Procurement); Maya Patel (ZenithCorp Legal); Ethan Wu (ZenithCorp Eng); Samira Khan (ZenithCorp Security)

Summary: Procurement lead walked through outstanding MSA/DPA redlines, legal asked about retention and audits, security wants KMS + audit logs. Redwood AE and SE explained hosting options, SLA language, and committed capacity pricing.

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood, I think we have Priya from the SE side as well, quick roll call?
[00:10] Jordan Lee: Jordan here for procurement, Maya from legal joining in a couple minutes, uh Ethan and Samira are on as well.
[00:18] Priya Sharma: Hi all, Priya, SE. I'll be the technical point for the pilot and the benchmark stuff.
[00:25] Alex Kim: Great. So agenda today: MSA and DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pricing/commits, and onboarding steps. We'll try to get through redlines and leave time for questions.

[02:05] Jordan Lee: Quick context, we have a procurement window for Q1 roll out, procurement needs pricing sign-off by end of month, legal needs to tidy the DPA/MSA. We're evaluating a couple vendors but Redwood has been recommended for inference performance.

[04:12] Maya Patel: Sorry a hair late, Maya here. We sent initial redlines to the MSA, a number of data residency clauses and liability caps, also a question on audit rights in the DPA.

[04:45] Alex Kim: Thanks Maya, yeah we saw the redlines. We can walk through them line by line, but high level: data residency we can offer region pinning for hosted, and for more strict requirements we can do Private/VPC deployment or Dedicated pools. Priya can describe the difference.

[05:20] Priya Sharma: Yeah, so hosted API gives fastest time to value, region pinning for EU/US is possible, but for full control we offer Redwood Private (customer VPC) or Dedicated (reserved GPU pools). Dedicated gives isolation and guaranteed throughput; Private gives you control of network and KMS.

[06:05] Samira Khan: For Security, the main items are KMS/HSM integration, customer-managed keys, access logs, and retention settings. Can Redwood support a bring-your-own-key model?

[06:28] Priya Sharma: Yes, BYOK is supported for Private and we have integrations for HSM/KMS. For Hosted we provide envelope encryption and we can do customer-managed keys in some enterprise plans.

[07:10] Maya Patel: On the DPA, audit rights — we need to be able to trigger an audit or get evidence for SOC2 within 30 days. Is that feasible?

[07:28] Alex Kim: We typically provide SOC2 Type II report and can provide evidence and a SOC package, we don't usually allow customer-triggered on-site audits for hosted customers, but for Dedicated/Private we can scope additional audit access. Priya will share the SOC2 and ISO docs.

[09:50] Jordan Lee: Liability cap — your redlines propose liability limited to fees paid in previous 12 months, our legal is asking for a higher cap for data breaches. Can we discuss?

[10:18] Maya Patel: Right, liability caps are a blocker, especially given the sensitive PII in our use case. We understand standard is fees paid, but we need a path to negotiation.

[11:05] Alex Kim: I hear you. We can take that back to legal — typical enterprise deals often add carve-outs for gross negligence, and for higher liability there's usually a higher enterprise plan or insurance-backed options. I'll flag this as a negotiation point.

[12:30] Priya Sharma: On SLA, we offer 99.9% uptime for the Dedicated and Private tiers with defined latency targets; hosted SLA is slightly lower but still competitive. For mission-critical we recommend Dedicated with canary rollouts, automatic fallback to hosted variants if the dedicated pool hits capacity.

[13:18] Ethan Wu: Can you clarify what the latency SLO looks like for our expected seq lengths? We're doing document summarization, average tokens per request about 1.2k and peak up to 4k.

[13:40] Priya Sharma: For 1.2k average and Dedicated pool we typically see median P95 latencies in the low 100s ms per token at scale, but the exact numbers depend on model and quantization. We should run a bench; if you share QPS and size we can give a targeted perf estimate.

[14:25] Jordan Lee: For pricing, procurement needs the committed capacity tiers and how bursts work — we have a long internal approval path.

[14:42] Alex Kim: We'll send a pricing spreadsheet: hosted per-token rates, embedding unit rates, and Dedicated reserved capacity monthly models with discounts at commit tiers. Bursting is allowed upto a defined percent with overage rates. We'll include an example invoice calculation.

[16:05] Maya Patel: Data retention — what's the default? And can we set retention to delete logs after X days?

[16:18] Priya Sharma: Default retention for transients is 30 days for hosted but can be configured. For Private/Dedicated you can set retention policies; we also support log redaction and the ability to opt-out of retention for certain routes.

[17:50] Samira Khan: Are API requests logged with any PII in them? We need assurances that logs won't contain raw PII and that any stored input is encrypted at rest.

[18:05] Alex Kim: We redact sensitive fields in logs by default and all data is encrypted at rest; we'll share the redaction doc. For extra assurance, Private deployment gives you control over network and key management.

[19:30] Jordan Lee: On the MSA redlines, there's a clause about subprocessing and subcontractors — we need visibility into who has access to data, esp for hosted deployments.

[19:46] Priya Sharma: We maintain a subcontractor list; for hosted we use cloud providers for infra and some managed services. We can provide a subprocessors list and, for Dedicated, limit subprocessors to a smaller set or switch to Private to eliminate cloud-managed infra access.

[21:00] Maya Patel: For the DPA retention / deletion obligations, we want a 30-day deletion SLA once contract terminates. Is that standard?

[21:18] Alex Kim: Yes, a 30-day post-termination deletion is standard in many of our enterprise contracts; we can confirm exact language and exceptions (e.g., legal holds).

[22:35] Ethan Wu: For onboarding, what's the standard timeline for a pilot with Dedicated capacity? We want to run a 4-week pilot with benchmarks.

[22:50] Priya Sharma: Pilot timeline: 1 week for provisioning Dedicated pool (if capacity available), 1 week for integration and smoke tests, 2 weeks for load/perf benchmarking and quality evals. So roughly 4 weeks end-to-end. If you start with hosted, it's typically faster.

[24:12] Jordan Lee: Procurement will need an SOW or onboarding addendum attached to the MSA that outlines the pilot scope and acceptance criteria.

[24:30] Alex Kim: We can include a short SOW with KPIs like throughput, P95 latency target, and cost threshold. Priya will draft an SOW template.

[26:00] Maya Patel: A couple legal asks: indemnity carve-outs, export control language, and clarity on choice of law. Preferred venue is Delaware, but we'll propose neutral arbitration.

[26:22] Alex Kim: We'll surface those to our legal team — usually choice of law is negotiable for enterprise deals; we'll include a proposed compromise.

[27:45] Jordan Lee: On pricing approvals — our finance needs a breakout: committed monthly cost, per-token overage, and sample monthly spend scenarios for 3, 6, 12 month commits.

[28:12] Alex Kim: Understood. We'll provide a workbook with examples and templates for capex/ocpex comparisons. Also will list discounts tied to commit size.

[29:50] Samira Khan: For compliance artifacts, beyond SOC2 we may request penetration test results or a summary. Do you provide that?

[30:10] Priya Sharma: We don't publish full pentest reports but we can provide a summary and we have a weekly pentest cadence with results available under NDA or in our security portal for enterprise customers.

[31:40] Maya Patel: On the DPA, we have a few redlines about subprocessor notice windows and breach notification timeframes (we want 48 hours). Can Redwood commit to that?

[32:00] Alex Kim: Our standard is 72 hours for incident notification, but we can discuss 48 hours for enterprise customers under specific plans — I'll note that as a negotiable item.

[33:15] Jordan Lee: For the final sign-off path, procurement will need: final MSA + DPA, approved pricing sheet, evidence of compliance (SOC2), and pilot SOW with acceptance criteria. Is that everything?

[33:40] Alex Kim: That sounds right. We'll prepare those artifacts.

[34:05] Priya Sharma: Quick technical note on KV cache and batching — to get cost efficiencies we'll recommend specific batching and prefix caching settings; we'll include recommended config for your workloads.

[35:20] Ethan Wu: For benchmarking, do you run ephemeral cache warmups or is that on our side? We need to make sure we measure steady-state cost.

[35:36] Priya Sharma: We'll collaborate on benchmark scripts; typically we do warmup runs and then measure steady-state. We'll include guidance and example scripts.

[36:50] Jordan Lee: Any other contractual items we should anticipate? We may ask for a demo of the console for the finance team to validate cost breakdowns.

[37:05] Alex Kim: Happy to do a finance-focused demo; show token-level cost and route breakdowns. We'll also include example dashboards showing per-route latency and spend.

[38:20] Maya Patel: One more thing — do you support SSO/SAML and RBAC for admin controls? We need to lock down multi-tenant access.

[38:40] Priya Sharma: Yes SSO (SAML) and SCIM provisioning supported for enterprise accounts; RBAC with roles and audit trails is available. We'll include a quick admin setup doc.

[39:55] Jordan Lee: Okay next steps recap?

[40:05] Alex Kim: Recap: Alex will send updated MSA + DPA with responses and highlight negotiable items; Priya will share SOC2, ISO summary, architecture diagram, and onboarding SOW; Alex will also send pricing workbook; customer to provide QPS and example payload sizes; schedule follow-up legal review.

[40:30] Maya Patel: Sounds good. We'll prioritize liability cap and breach notification during redlines.

[41:10] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone, we'll target those deliverables this week and set up the next call for 2025-11-26 for legal review. Appreciate the time.
[41:24] Jordan Lee: Thanks all.

[41:32] Meeting end: 15:42 UTC
